text: Agent tutorial: an automated code reviewer, written as a doeff program.
The program does not start Claude Code itself. It yields effects, and the handler around it decides how each one is met.
A review needs four effects: launch a session, await its result, follow up, and stop it.
Step one: the review as a program. review file yields the four effects.
Calling it only builds the program. Nothing runs until a handler answers its effects.
Launch session goes out, and the handler resumes the program with a session handle.
Await result waits in one step. Waiting is the handler's job, so there is no polling loop and no sleep.
The outcome comes back: the agent exited, with a result checked against the schema.
Stop session sits in a finally block, so the session is stopped on every path.
Step two: a test handler. The handler decorator makes a function of the effect and k into a handler.
k is the rest of the program. Resume k with a value, and the program goes on with that value as the result of its yield.
The annotation names the effects it takes. Any other effect goes past it, to the next handler out.
Under scripted agent, the review returns approve, and the log reads launch, await, stop.
review file did not change for the test. The test chose the handler.
Step three: when the agent does not finish, the script plays the other outcomes.
The agent stops to ask. The program sends a follow up, awaits again, and gets the review.
Nothing comes back within the timeout, and review file raises review failed.
A result that does not match the schema comes back with the reason, and review file raises too.
On every path, the finally block stops the session.
Step four: several files. Spawn starts a task per file, and Gather collects the results in order.
Each effect goes to its own handler: the scheduler, try handler, and the scripted agent.
A semaphore of two lets at most two reviews hold a session. The scripted agent answers at once, so here they run one after another.
Try turns the timeout of b dot py into an Err value, so one failure does not stop the others.
All three sessions are stopped, the failed one too.
Step five: doeff agents ships a test handler of the same kind, the scenario agent handler.
The same review file returns request changes, with one issue, from the scripted step.
Step six: in production, daemon agent handlers send the same effects to the session host.
The host starts Claude Code in a terminal, watches it, checks its result against the schema, and stops it.
The programs never changed. Only the handlers did.
The program says what it needs. The handler decides how: a script in a test, Claude Code in production.
